Subject: Dedicated GPU recommendation + cost/perf heuristics (Delta Health)

Hi Sana / Delta ops team —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Per our conversation, I attached a concise proposal that outlines three viable Dedicated fleet options and the heuristics we used to pick a primary SKU for your workload. Short summary up-top:

- Recommendation: H100-80GB reserved pool for your realtime API plus a small L4 burst pool for cheap short-context inference.
- Rationale: H100 gives best tokens/sec for long-context clinical summarization (20k tokens session) and larger KV cache headroom. L4 is cost-effective for low-latency, short queries (under 2k tokens).
- Cost metric we optimized: tokens-per-dollar under your 95th-pct latency SLO target (150ms tail for short calls, 800ms tail for long sessions).

Attachments: Delta_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf, inference-benchmarks-070125.csv (benchmark harness + raw numbers).

Action items: can you confirm the split you expect between long-context summarization vs short query traffic (ballpark %)? We used 65/35 in the deck but want to validate before finalizing commit sizing. Also flag any procurement timing constraints — we can stage capacity in two weeks if needed.

Thanks,

1) Traffic mix: our weekly aggregate is closer to 55% short queries, 45% long sessions, but peak business hours skew long sessions up to ~60%. We should model both baseline and peak for commitment sizing.

Thanks for looping me in — adding a few operational notes and the concurrency math we ran to justify the H100 pick.

Key assumptions we used (see attached CSV for microbenchmarks):
- Model: open-llm-v2-70b (float16 runtime).
- Average generation rate: H100 ~420 tokens/sec, A100 ~260 tokens/sec, L4 ~120 tokens/sec (measured at batch size 1; multi-request batching increases effective throughput approx 1.8x for H100/A100 under our workload patterns).
- KV cache per long session: peak 18GB; working set after tokenization ~22GB with metadata.
- Concurrency target: 40 long sessions simultaneously at 95th percentile peak (this matches Delta's traffic spike profile).

Memory math (H100 80GB):
- 40 sessions * 22GB = 880GB total KV across sessions. We use multiplexed KV slotting across GPUs with per-slot compression and shard layout. With 32-way tiling and 1.1x compression amortization, effective per-GPU headroom required = ~28GB. So an 80GB H100 yields ~2.8x headroom factor vs per-gpu working set and supports our concurrency target with room for cache growth and replication for high-availability.

Why not A100? Two reasons: 1) A100 40GB forces much higher tiling (reduces batching efficiency and increases cross-GPU sync overhead) and 2) for long sessions A100's tokens/sec at the given batch characteristics creates an unacceptable tail latency.

Where L4 fits: low-cost concurrent pool for short queries (stateless, small context) — we recommend setting an autoscale-based burst policy to spill to L4 for non-cached / non-long-context requests. That reduces cost during baseline traffic.

Operational risks and mitigations:
- Risk: H100 inventory and price volatility. Mitigation: negotiate a 12-16 week price lock and include preemptible burst credits (we can define a fallthrough to compatible A100 pool if H100 capacity constrained).
- Risk: over-provisioning for KV-heavy pathological sessions. Mitigation: implement session admission control + progressive offload to NVMe cache when needed.

Action suggestions for procurement/SOW:
1) Commit to base H100 pool sized for 60 long-session concurrency and a small L4 pool for 200 concurrent short requests.
2) Include explicit fallback to A100 with throttling controls in the SLA.
3) Add a 6-week pilot window to validate real traffic and re-balance before annual commit.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Sana — quick technical note on the headroom and tokens-per-dollar heuristic so procurement/legal have a plain-English line item for the SOW:

Tokens-per-dollar summary (simple model):
- Metric = (tokens/sec * effective_hours_per_day * utilization_factor * 3600) / hourly_cost_of_gpu
- Using our measured microbenchmarks and Delta's profile: H100 gives ~2.1x tokens-per-dollar vs A100 for long-session workloads when you account for reduced cross-GPU overhead and better batching at the same tail latency target. L4 is ~0.5x for long sessions but ~3.4x for short single-turn queries (low context) because of much lower per-hour cost.

SOW bullet to include for legal/procurement: 
"Committed pool: H100-80GB N GPUs to support X concurrent long sessions (95th pct). Delta will be billed at reserved H100 rate; Redwood will provide L4 burst capacity at specified consumption rates. A fallback policy and reallocation window (72 hours) will be documented if H100 inventory constraints require temporary A100 fallback. Pilot metrics and acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 800ms for long sessions, p95 latency <= 150ms for short queries, end-to-end correctness on 95% of eval prompt set.

We can also produce a short 1-pager for legal that describes the tokens-per-dollar heuristic and the concurrency formula if that helps.

Thanks,
Dev

Redwood Inference
